processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Raw materials of high purity (>99.9 %) melted in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere to produce Fe-35Mn-xAl-5Cu (x = 19) ingots.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: rolled into plates of 4 mm thickness
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
Solution-treated sample aged at 575 °C for 10 h, followed by water quenching. This is the terminal condition of the target sample.

structures.overall_structure: After aging the 19Al (Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu) alloy at 575 °C for 10 h the microstructure is a largely/essentially β-Mn transformed matrix containing fine new precipitates (BCC phase and FCC Cu-rich phase) located between the β-Mn regions; the SE image for this condition shows a β-Mn matrix with fine 'new precipitates'. β-Mn precipitation in 19Al is slower than in 15Al/17Al, first appearing along α grain boundaries.

phases_present.morphology: fine new precipitates at β-Mn interfaces
fine new precipitates at β-Mn interfaces (FCC twins observed in the Cu-rich particles)

precipitates.distribution: at the interfaces between β-Mn (comparable size distribution to the FCC Cu-rich phase)
at the interfaces between β-Mn; fine particles with FCC twins

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase (microstructure evolution sequence for Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels during aging). For the 19Al alloy the α→β-Mn transformation is slow: at 525 °C only a small amount (12.1 %) of β-Mn forms after 10 h; at 575 °C β-Mn first appears along α grain boundaries and residual α persists at short times.
interfaces.interface_notes: The FCC Cu-rich phase is Cu-rich and depleted in Fe and Mn with FCC twins frequently observed within the particles; the β-Mn is poor in Cu (TEM on the 15Al/17Al hardest samples). The fine BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates sit between the β-Mn interfaces in the ultra-hard alloys and their fraction increases with Al content while the FCC Cu-rich fraction decreases.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester at a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the average reported.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N, dwell 15 s, 5 measurements averaged per sample
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Vickers hardness of the aged samples and build hardness-aging contour maps
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 19Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 10 h has a hardness of 843.7 ± 7.9 HV; hardness values of 19Al span 263.8 HV (solution-treated) to 917.8 HV (600 °C/10 h).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Image the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) and new precipitates after aging
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 9 shows that for 19Al at 575 °C/10 h the SE image is a β-Mn matrix with fine 'new precipitates'; β-Mn in 19Al first appears along α grain boundaries and the transformation is slow.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Scanning step size 1.5 μm (low magnification) and 0.05 μm (high magnification)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phases and the α→β-Mn transformation plus new BCC/FCC precipitates after aging
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated alloys are single-phase α (BCC); aging transforms α to β-Mn with new BCC and FCC phases. For 19Al (Figs. 3 and 6) the EBSD phase maps show the α→β-Mn transformation advancing with aging temperature and the emergence of new BCC and FCC precipitates.

characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase compositions of the alloys
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 19Al alloy aged at 550 °C for 6 h shows both α-Mn and β-Mn diffraction peaks (together with α/D0₃), indicating α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitated during aging before full transformation to β-Mn.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Talos F200X microscope equipped with an EDS detector, operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate the fine precipitates at β-Mn interfaces and identify the Cu-rich FCC phase
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fine FCC Cu-rich particles (with FCC twins) form at the β-Mn interfaces; β-Mn is poor in Cu (TEM on the 15Al 600 °C/6 h and 17Al 575 °C/6 h hardest samples).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Indentation depth 200 nm; test points spaced ≥ 5 μm apart; samples mechanically polished
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the intrinsic hardness of β-Mn and of the FCC Cu-rich/BCC precipitates in the hardest samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: The hardest 19Al sample (600 °C/10 h) shows an average nanoindentation hardness of 10.4 ± 1.3 GPa and a β-Mn intrinsic hardness of 12.5 ± 0.4 GPa (β-Mn Al content 17.5 at.%).

unmapped_findings: For the 19Al alloy the optimal aging temperature range to achieve ultra-high hardness is 575–625 °C, and the peak Vickers hardness (917.8 ± 24.5 HV) is reached at 600 °C for 10 h — a sibling aging condition, not the 575 °C/10 h sample (b0032, b0038).

Fracture toughness KIC of the hardest Fe-Mn-Al-Cu samples (indentation technique, Eq. 1) is 8.6 MPa·m^1/2 (15Al, 965.6 HV), 6.6 MPa·m^1/2 (17Al, 924.9 HV) and 3.5 MPa·m^1/2 (19Al, 917.8 HV); the 3.5 MPa·m^1/2 value belongs to the 19Al peak-hardness sample (600 °C/10 h), not the 575 °C/10 h sample (b0021, b0061).
The elastic modulus of the 19Al alloy is 181 GPa (from compressive stress-strain curves), used together with the elastic moduli 164 GPa (15Al) and 175 GPa (17Al) in Eq. 1 for KIC evaluation (b0023).

The intrinsic hardness of β-Mn in the hardest 19Al sample (600 °C/10 h) is 12.5 ± 0.4 GPa from nanoindentation (areas not contacting FCC Cu-rich/BCC phases); SEM-EDS gives β-Mn composition Mn 36.2, Al 17.5, Cu 2.6 at.% (b0060, figure_014).

For the 19Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 6 h, the volume fraction of the FCC Cu-rich + BCC precipitates between β-Mn interfaces is 6.5 %; the fraction increases with Al content (15Al: 3.9 % at 650 °C/3 h; 17Al: 4.7 % at 650 °C/10 h) (b0069).

When the 19Al alloy was aged at 525 °C for 10 h only 12.1 % β-Mn precipitated, resulting in a minimal increase in hardness; after aging at 650 °C for 6 h the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn with a large amount of new BCC phase (b0041).
The 19Al alloy EDS-measured chemical composition is Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 at.% (Table 1).
An ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g was achieved in the Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu (15Al) low-density steel — a sibling alloy, not the 19Al sample (b0077).
